prompt: Vertical 9:16 photograph shot on 35 mm colour-negative film at night in heavy London rain, taken from inside the cab of a UK box ambulance built on a large panel van, the camera just behind and well above the right-hand driver's shoulder so we look steeply down through a tall, almost upright windscreen at the wet road. A few metres ahead and clearly below our eye-line, a police motorcycle outrider sits astride a white touring motorbike, white helmet with a dark visor, fluorescent yellow waterproof jacket with a blue-and-yellow chequered band, holding one black-gloved palm flat up towards us: stop. Behind him an empty, cleared junction of shiny tarmac and a single red traffic light glowing through the rain. Lower frame: the broad, flat, shelf-like van dashboard in dark grey plastic, a coiled radio handset clipped to it, a dark-screened data terminal on a black swing arm angled towards the driver showing only a soft unreadable glow, and the driver's hands in black nitrile gloves on a big van steering wheel set almost flat, sleeves of a dark green paramedic uniform. Wipers parked at the bottom of the glass, raindrops beaded across it. Light sources: our own blue roof strobes washing the wet bonnet edge and his hi-vis in cold blue, the twin blue lights on his bike, the red traffic signal, sodium-orange street lamps above the junction, and the faint amber glow of the dashboard instruments. Teal shadows, visible film grain, slight halation round every light, natural faces and hands, no readable text, plates, logos or lettering anywhere. Thanks.

Vertical 9:16 night photograph on grainy 35 mm colour-negative stock, a real documentary frame, taken from far back in the cab of a UK front-line ambulance, from the doorway in the bulkhead behind the seats, so both front seats, the headrests and the roof-mounted grab handle frame the view: a high, boxy van cab with a huge upright windscreen streaked with rain. The paramedic driver sits on the right, seen from behind, dark green uniform, one gloved hand on top of the wide, flat-angled steering wheel, the other lifted off it in a half-shrug of disbelief. The whole width of the plain van dashboard runs across the frame: a radio handset on its curly cord, a small sat-nav on a suction mount, a rugged data terminal on a jointed arm glowing a faint green, nothing legible. Out through the glass and well below us on the drenched road, a police motorcycle outrider in a fluorescent yellow jacket with a blue-and-yellow chequer pattern and a white helmet has stopped his white bike side-on across our path, gloved hand raised high. Beyond him a cleared crossroads, a red traffic light, sodium street lamps. A wiper is caught mid-sweep, blurred, cutting an arc through the water. Lights: our blue roof strobe bouncing off the wet bonnet and his reflective jacket, his bike's flashing blue lamps, the red signal, orange sodium lamps, the dim instrument glow lighting the driver's knuckles. Cold teal shadows, halation, film grain, natural hands with five fingers, no text, plates, signs or logos. Thanks.
